reuse.why: Reuses link.findOrCreateBank, bankSync.syncAccount, handleSyncResponse and the shared balance branch for Fintegra, and routes all six providers through one precondition helper, but re-writes unlinkAccount's field clearing and copies the Akahu link/download bodies rather than sharing them.

duplication.why: linkFintegraAccount is a near-verbatim copy of linkAkahuAccount, downloadFintegraTransactions a verbatim copy of downloadAkahuTransactions, and the local-unlink db.updateAccount block copies unlinkAccount's update.

placement.why: Link rules sit in one pre-link helper in accounts/app.ts, the download in sync.ts and the URL in server-config.ts, matching where the tree puts each kind of logic.

scope.why: Everything maps to one of the four steps; tests cover only the closed-account rule, and the Fintegra link also widens the success event's tables, a small unrequested divergence from its template.

maintainability.why: The precondition helper is a single point for the link rules, but it is still named assertBankAccountNotLinked while it now unlinks other accounts when a flag is set, and the per-provider copies multiply the code a maintainer must keep in step.

bypasses_abstraction.where: assertBankAccountNotLinked in accounts/app.ts clears the holder with its own db.updateAccount instead of sharing the local part of unlinkAccount.

disguised_duplication.where: The Fintegra link/download functions and the clearing block are literal copies (provider names swapped), not reshaped.

abstraction_drift.where: assertBankAccountNotLinked (created in step 1) gains a replaceExistingLink parameter and a branch that mutates other accounts, turning an assertion into a side-effecting claim without a rename; all six provider link functions still call it.
